specific_prose_corrections: Input/output meaning precedes loss and derivative. Physical input divided by a reference amount, neural intermediate values, parameter ordering and response units are explicit.
The zero-activation hand point explains each parameter route; shared error multiplication adds both paths, and finite differences perturb one parameter at a time.
Training uses numerical reference coordinates and average half-square gradients while the plot reports MSE. Fixed curves, preview parameters and training are distinguished.
Fixed-interval state samples define n, current/next pairing and external inputs. The three-feature least-squares fit is accurately described.
The rollout error decomposition separates propagation of past state bias from local mapping error. Stored one-step versus rollout parameter choices and held-out ordering are reported.
Continuous states, continuous observation objectives, Euler states/objectives and their sensitivities are separate. Observation pairs and gradient objects are defined before use.
The adjoint is motivated by future-loss dependence; product differentiation, residual jumps, before/after time notation, and piecewise integrals are explained with a two-step discrete example.
Negative-step Euler reconstruction is contrasted with algebraic inversion; its error is not folded into a claim about exact continuous adjoints.
The nonlinear ODE amplitude example uses grid search on a fixed Euler mesh, and its new-initial result is relative to that same discrete generator.
Fixed PINN candidates, shared observation/collocation times and reference plotting grid are described according to actual execution. Data, equation and initial losses carry separate units and scales.
The diffusion candidate is a concentration deviation; physical length normalization, amplitude reference, paired points, heatmap axes/scales, endpoint derivatives and sx initial changes are explicit.

Hybrid input rates differ from discrete per-step amounts. Mechanism parameters stay fixed during the single-amplitude search; its initial-inclusive metric and capstone initial-excluding metric are stated.
A linear correction has different units from the tanh amplitude. Parameter-difference invariance, nonzero-state independent flux and weighted candidate spread are connected by hand examples.
The capstone uses a fixed candidate amplitude, not another fit. Its error statistics and separate gradient/loss-scale exercises are accurately described.

All 48 question statements/contracts stand independently. List/tuple order, sample record fields, initial inclusion and zero input versus empty input are explicit; answer/option identities are preserved.

Chapter prerequisites use the needed prior knowledge rather than expanding new chapter concepts as prerequisites. Five web views share notebook notation and label state derivatives separately from loss gradients.
